metadata.description: LADC 2026 final completion campaign. Fills the genuinely empty cells of the MNIST block-width sweep and pins the timeout-sensitivity crossover. Designed to finish inside one day on a single machine.

finding_1_why_the_cells_are_empty.root_cause: The 13 missing MNIST beta=0/beta=10 cells in output/ladc2026_matrix_runs did not time out on complexity. They crashed on 'ValueError: Exceeds the limit (4300) for integer string conversion' raised by _assumption_box_cardinality, a diagnostic-only int-to-str formatting call on a box whose cardinality is around 2^10000.
finding_1_why_the_cells_are_empty.status: Fixed in commit c9a9745 (src/synthesis/preqbmc.py, the except ValueError branch that now returns a truthful '>=2^k' lower bound). Verified by calling the function directly on a 784-dimensional box: it returns without raising.
finding_1_why_the_cells_are_empty.implication: These configurations are runnable again with no further code change. An assumed timeout must never be reported as a measured timeout.

finding_2_the_300s_budget_is_the_binding.measurement: The monolithic (beta=0) MNIST 1blk_10 layer query needs about 465 s. Under a 300 s budget it times out, and the bit-width search then burns 17-25 further queries at 300 s each (1.5-2.1 h per run) without ever reaching a verdict. Under a 1200 s budget the same configuration verifies the first width (Q13_F8) and the whole run costs 511 s with 13 queries and zero timeouts.
finding_2_the_300s_budget_is_the_binding.consequence_for_this_campaign: Every run here uses a 1200 s per-query budget. That is what makes the campaign fit in a day: it converts ~2 h of wasted timeout churn per run into ~0.15 h of productive solving.
finding_2_the_300s_budget_is_the_binding.consequence_for_the_paper: The existing 'monolithic times out' result is an artefact of the 300 s budget, not evidence of a complexity wall. Arm F4 measures that dependence directly instead of hiding it. The beta=0 cells produced here are at 1200 s and are NOT comparable to the existing 300 s beta in {1,2,5} cells on the time axis; state the budget in any table that mixes them.

finding_3_beta10_equals_beta0_for_width1.proof_by_code: _hidden_block_ranges(output_size) returns [(0, output_size)] when esbmc_layer_block_size <= 0, and [(0, 10)] when the block size is 10 and output_size is 10. The partitions are identical.
finding_3_beta10_equals_beta0_for_width1.proof_by_artifact: The generated harnesses layers/blocks/layer_0_block_0_n0_10_Q13_F8.c (beta=10) and layers/layer_0_Q13_F8.c (beta=0) for mnist 1blk_10 eps=0.25 differ by zero lines.
finding_3_beta10_equals_beta0_for_width1.affected: 1blk_10 has 10 output neurons and each layer of 2blk_10_10 has 10 output neurons, so beta=10 is the monolithic configuration for both. 1blk_25 is NOT affected: beta=10 partitions 25 neurons into [(0,10),(10,20),(20,25)], three genuine blocks.
finding_3_beta10_equals_beta0_for_width1.consequence: An earlier draft of this campaign requested beta=10 for 1blk_10 and 2blk_10_10 as if they were separate cells. Those 9 runs were dropped: they are duplicates of beta=0 and, for 2blk_10_10, expensive duplicates. One beta=10 run is retained (arm F1b) purely to demonstrate the equivalence empirically.
finding_3_beta10_equals_beta0_for_width1.consequence_for_the_paper: The 1blk_10 and 2blk_10_10 block-width sweeps have four distinct settings, not five: beta in {0 == 10, 1, 2, 5}. Presenting beta=0 and beta=10 as independent columns for these architectures would overstate the sweep. Say so in the caption.

cost_model.basis: Measured from output/ladc2026_mnist_timeout_escalation_runs, output/ladc2026_matrix_runs and output/article_runs_* for matched architectures.
cost_model.mnist_1blk_10_beta0: 511 s (13 queries, 0 timeouts) at to=1200; 441 s at to=1800
cost_model.mnist_1blk_10_beta10: 430 s at to=900 (equivalent configuration, see finding_3)
cost_model.mnist_1blk_25_beta0: unmeasured above 300 s; timed out at 302 s/1 query under to=300, peak 0.55 GiB
cost_model.mnist_1blk_25_beta10: unmeasured above 300 s; timed out at 680 s/3 queries under to=300, peak 0.60 GiB
cost_model.mnist_2blk_10_10_beta0: unmeasured. beta in {1,2,5} cost 2600-3900 s at to=300 with peaks to 6.14 GiB. This is the dominant wall-clock risk and carries the tightest cap.
cost_model.memory_headroom: Worst MNIST peak observed anywhere is 6.14 GiB (2blk_10_10) and 11.0 GiB (1blk_100 frontier, not in this campaign). The machine has 25 GiB total and about 17 GiB available, so the 20 GiB per-query limit is retained for comparability with existing runs and is not expected to bind. Wall-clock caps, not the memory limit, are the budget guard.
cost_model.units_note: expected_cost_seconds on each run entry is the total for that entry across all of its expanded runs. runner_timeout_seconds is a cap on EACH expanded run, not on the entry. So the 5-run entry ladc_f3_mnist_2blk10_monolithic expects 12500 s in total but could consume up to 5 x 3600 = 18000 s before its caps fire.
cost_model.hard_cap_note: runner_timeout_seconds caps each expanded run. A capped run is recorded as a failure and the campaign continues because allowed_failure is true everywhere. A capped run is an honest missing cell, not a timeout result, and must not be reported as one.

metadata.ordering_rationale: Groups are listed cheapest-and-highest-value first. If the campaign is stopped early the cells that matter most already exist. Arm F1 alone completes the headline monolithic-versus-blockwise comparison for 1blk_10, and arm F4 alone answers the reviewer's timeout question.
metadata.verify_before_launch: Run --dry-run first and confirm each emitted command carries --esbmc-timeout-seconds 1200 (600 for the two F4 sensitivity entries). The runner also exposes its own --esbmc-timeout-seconds flag defaulting to 900; do not pass it, or it may override the per-run budgets this campaign depends on.

runs.name: ladc_f1_mnist_1blk10_monolithic
runs.notes: Completes the monolithic column of the 1blk_10 block-width sweep across the full epsilon frontier. Highest value per hour in the campaign: this is the beta=0 baseline the reviewer asked for, and it is known to verify in 511 s at this budget. 5 runs.

runs.name: ladc_f1b_mnist_1blk10_beta10_equivalence_check
runs.notes: Single run retained to demonstrate empirically what finding_3 proves statically: for a 10-neuron layer, beta=10 and beta=0 are the same configuration and should produce the same verdict, query count and harness. Compare against ladc_f1_mnist_1blk10_monolithic_eps0p25_full_layer. 1 run.

runs.name: ladc_f2_mnist_1blk25_sample3
runs.notes: 1blk_25 monolithic and beta=10. Both are genuine distinct cells here because 25 neurons split into three blocks at beta=10. Both timed out under 300 s (302 s/1 query and 680 s/3 queries), so this is the first measurement of either above the single-query requirement. 2 runs.

runs.name: ladc_f2_mnist_1blk25_sample2228
runs.notes: Second 1blk_25 sample, matching the epsilon (0.25) and cohort of the existing beta in {1,2,5} cells. 2 runs.

runs.name: ladc_f2_mnist_1blk25_sample9389
runs.notes: Third 1blk_25 sample, matching the epsilon (0.25) and cohort of the existing beta in {1,2,5} cells. 2 runs.

runs.name: ladc_f3_mnist_2blk10_monolithic
runs.notes: DOMINANT RISK IN THE CAMPAIGN. Two-layer monolithic column. beta in {1,2,5} cost 2600-3900 s each at to=300 with peaks to 6.14 GiB, and the deeper neighbour 2blk_25_25 beta=0 cost 8830-9073 s at to=900. The 3600 s cap bounds the damage: if a cell is cut off it is recorded as a failure and the campaign continues. Disable this entry first if the clock is tight, because F1, F2 and F4 already answer the reviewer table. 5 runs.

runs.name: ladc_f4_timeout_crossover_1blk10_beta0_to600
runs.notes: THE SINGLE MOST VALUABLE RUN FOR THE TIMEOUT QUESTION. The monolithic query needs about 465 s. It is already known to TIMEOUT at 300 s and to VERIFY at 1200 s (511 s, 13 queries). A 600 s budget brackets the crossover and shows the 300 s result is a budget artefact rather than a complexity wall. 1 run.

runs.name: ladc_f4_timeout_sensitivity_1blk10_beta2_eps0p5_to600
runs.notes: Unresolved beta=2 region (MARGIN_INCONCLUSIVE at 300 s, 382.5 s, zero timeout blocks and zero failed blocks) rerun at double the budget. Expected to remain MARGIN_INCONCLUSIVE, which is precisely the point: it shows the inconclusive verdicts are precision limits of the derived margin, not solver limits. 1 run.

runs.name: ladc_f4_timeout_sensitivity_1blk10_beta2_eps0p5_to1200
runs.notes: Same unresolved region at four times the original budget. Together with the 300 s result already on disk this yields a three-point budget ladder at fixed beta, which is the evidence the timeout justification needs. 1 run.

runs.name: ladc_f5_frontier_mnist_1blk100_monolithic
runs.notes: DISABLED ON PURPOSE. The 1blk_100 frontier is not needed to answer the reviewer table and the evidence says it is expensive: the beta=1 frontier run cost 3260 s with 120 queries and 11228 MiB, and a 1blk_100 beta=10 run elsewhere cost 17164 s and still FAILED. Enable with --include-disabled only if the rest of the campaign finishes early.
